top.title: Come for the science, stay for the big iron: Supercomputer admin on why he loves the job
top.description: Web hosting might seem like an unlikely on-ramp to supercomputer administration, but it set Mark O'Shea on his way to running some of Australia's most powerful machines. O'Shea is team leader for supercomputing operations and senior supercomputing systems administrator at Australia's Pawsey Supercomputing Research Centre . Pawsey is home to Setonix, an HPE Cray EX supercomputer with more than 200,000 AMD EPYC CPU cores and hundreds of AMD Instinct MI250X accelerators. Its GPU partition ranks 87th in the November TOP500 and 37th in the Green500 , which measures computational performance per watt. "Working in web hosting wasn't much different to what I was doing a few years later with supercomputers," O'Shea tells The Register . "Datacenters are essentially several thousand computers, as are supercomputers. "So, we essentially had the same problems," he says, especially as regards cooling and power management. There's no single formal route into supercomputer administration in Australia, O'Shea says. He picked up the necessary skills over time. Andrew Underwood, Dell's chief technology officer for high-performance computing and artificial intelligence across the Asia-Pacific, Japan, and China, says that lack of formal training means some supercomputer admins start in academia. He's observed that many HPC admins emerge from the sciences, catching the computing bug during their studies. A biologist working with a massive genomics database, for example, might discover a taste for running the systems behind it. "The biologist might decide they want to be someone working in IT helping other biologists transform their industry," Underwood says . "One of the things I really admire about people who work in the supercomputing field is they take it so seriously," Underwood adds. "It's almost a passion, a hobby, more so than it is a job." "They want to play that real supporting and foundational role of assisting and engaging with scientists to help them use the technology to solve the problems the world faces." O'Shea agrees, noting that many people who get into supercomputer admin are PhD graduates who stick around their universities after they graduate. Some of them gravitate toward running the departmental computers and then wind up in supercomputing. "There are many roles around universities allowing people to be introduced to [supercomputer administration] while still doing enterprise-style or more departmental admin for researchers and system administration," O'Shea says. Regardless of how a supercomputer admin gets their gig, both O'Shea and Underwood say the supersysadmin community is tight knit – which may not always be a good thing. "As an industry in supercomputing, we need to be open to people from diverse backgrounds," Underwood says, "and we need to build these frameworks like the Student Cluster Competition, conferences like eResearch and the SC Conference, where students can get educated and systems admins get exposed to continual training." top.description: Leeds United head-wrecking crew stay the right side of crazy at Chelsea - Graham Smyth's Verdict It's good to be just the right side of crazy. More often than not Leeds United Football Club finds itself involved in mayhem. That is an apt word for so much of all that has happened to and around this club since its very inception in 1919. There's been good crazy and bad crazy, everything from the daft to the scarcely believable. Leeds United is a club that rarely needs a second invitation to lose the run of itself. Even under the calm managerial control of Daniel Farke and the sober ownership of 49ers Enterprises, minds have melted and chaos has briefly reigned at times. Take, for example, the last trip to Stamford Bridge, when Leeds lost 6-3. Scorelines like that rarely make sense. That was, in the words of Jayden Bogle, a 'crazy game' and something that he wanted to put right. And what better way to do that than a good old-fashioned historical head-wrecking. It all started with a bit of cat and mouse. Leeds almost played rope-a-dope in the opening stages, seeing relatively little of the football and absorbing pressure. Chelsea saw precious little of James Trafford's goal, because Leeds stayed so compact and patient, looking for opportunities to nip in. Farke's three centre-backs all chipped in with important interventions but almost all of the defending was kept to the edge of the area and further out. It wasn't until the 14th minute that the hosts mustered a shot, Morgan Rogers pulling the trigger from distance and missing the target. Chances to break out were few and far between, but when Leeds did get hold of the ball they moved it well. So well in fact that they created two good opportunities to open the scoring. James Justin's cross from the right was perfect for Dominic Calvert-Lewin and his header was so close to perfect - only the crossbar saved Chelsea. Quick, slick football unlocked space on the left and Noah Okafor's cross was headed downwards by Calvert-Lewin and Emiliano Martinez held on. Having worked so hard to break Chelsea's spell of territorial dominance, conceding an opener will have annoyed Farke. A second source of chagrin was the manner of the concession. One long ball, one lost aerial duel, a missed handball, one pass to the left and a shot seared inside Trafford's near post. The keeper appeared to be well positioned but was simply unable to get a hand on a thunderously-struck shot. Leeds responded to the goal not only with annoyance, but like it was a grievous personal slight. The response was pure manic aggression. The first goal came three minutes after Chelsea's. top.title: Macau GP: Kean Nakamura-Berta takes win after Enzo Deligny crashes out
top.description: Motorsport photo Kean Nakamura-Berta claimed a comfortable Macau Grand Prix victory after forcing early leader Enzo Deligny into a mistake at Lisboa. It was a tricky first few corners for the drivers starting on the front row as second-placed Mattia Colnaghi struggled to get away, while polesitter Rashid Al Dhaheri was immediately under attack. Deligny braved it around the outside of the Mercedes junior at Mandarin to grab the lead, before Al Dhaheri then lost out to both Nakamura-Berta and Yuki Sano on the run to Lisboa. Williams junior Nakamura-Berta spent the next couple of laps putting Deligny under pressure before a brief safety car period was triggered when ninth-placed Reza Seewooruthun was tapped into the barriers out of Mandarin by last year's F4 World Cup winner Jules Roussel. Nakamura-Berta continued to remain about half a second behind Deligny upon the restart until he suddenly closed on lap 10 of 16. The SJM Theodore Racing driver was right on the tail of Deligny on the run to Lisboa and the leader left his braking as late as he dared but it was too late and he ploughed into the barriers. This gifted Nakamura-Berta a huge 3.5s lead, which enabled him to stroke it home to the flag to take the victory. The British-born Japanese, Slovak driver, who was third in this year's Formula Regional European Championship standings, made up for the disappointment of crashing out of the F4 World Cup last year. His large margin was aided by R-ace GP driver Al Dhaheri spending several laps bottled up behind Sano's TOM'S Formula Regional machine. The qualification race winner eventually found a way through around the outside of Mandarin on lap 12 but there was too much for him to do to close on Nakamura-Berta in the remaining three tours. Alex Ninovic Alex Ninovic Alex Ninovic made a similar move on Sano at Mandarin on the following lap to return to his starting spot of third on the grid. The 2025 GB3 champion then set about battling Al Dhaheri, blasting ahead on the run to Mandarin on the final lap to finish second, 2.456s behind the winner. Nakamura-Berta's team-mate James Egozi also passed Sano in the closing stages to seal fourth. Sano then lost out to fellow Japanese racer Taito Kato (ART Grand Prix) on the last lap but proceeded to plough into Kato at Lisboa as he attempted to retaliate, with the unsighted Matteo De Palo collecting them. This meant Alex Powell (Prema) and Ernesto Rivera (Van Amersfoort Racing) completed the top six, while Colnaghi was eventually classified 11th after his startline strife. top.title: 'Not the right time' - Fernandes pauses Man Utd contract talks
top.description: Bruno Fernandes has scored in each of his past two games for Manchester United [EPA] Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes says he has been offered a new contract by the club but feels it "is not the right time" for discussions about his future. The 32-year-old midfielder is out of contract at the end of the season , though the club have the option to trigger a 12-month extension until 2028. He was left out of the side under previous manager Michael Carrick but says he has no issues at the club and has chosen to stay at Old Trafford despite offers elsewhere in recent seasons. He told Sky Sports: "The club offered me a new contract, so I think that, from their side, shows that they want me to stay. "There's no negotiations ongoing, but I've seen people saying that 'he's asked for more money, he's asked for more years'. If I wanted more money, I wouldn't be here. "I had somewhere to go to get much more money than being at Manchester United. I could have been in a place that is much warmer than Manchester. "Two summers ago, three summers ago, last summer, I always had the chance to leave and I always chose to be here." United chief executive Omar Berrada recently spoke about Fernandes' contract situation, saying: "It's true that we're having conversations about his new contract, but I prefer to keep that private." Fernandes has scored 75 Premier League goals since signing from Sporting in 2020 and last season set a record for the most assists in a Premier League season. His form has tailed off this season in a poor start for the club as a whole. United are 19th in the Premier League table going into Mauricio Pochettino's first game in charge against rivals Liverpool on Sunday afternoon. "We spoke about the contract at the end of last season," Fernandes said. "We came in at the beginning of this season speaking about the contract, but about the context of the team and the club, I just put that to a side because I don't think it's the right moment, neither for me, nor for the club, to be talking about negotiations. "The most important thing now is that the club gets back to winning games." 'He will see what Man Utd are made of' - Pulis on Pochettino's first game No fallout with Carrick Fernandes was dropped for the Premier League defeat by Bournemouth last month after being critical of United's approach in their heavy defeat against Como in the Champions League. But Fernandes says he did not fall out with Carrick, who was sacked on 12 November. "The manager came to speak to me before the Bournemouth game, to say: 'Look, I'm not going to start you tomorrow. There's nothing to do with the words of Como, I know people will make it around that. I just want to tell you that we need to change something, I need to make a change, performances have not been great, so I just want you to know that there's nothing to do with that'," Fernandes said. top.title: How lessons from football history reveal the real reason behind Manchester City’s decline
top.description: The best part of five hours after the final whistle blew at the Etihad Stadium and about 150 miles north east, Noni Madueke scored an equaliser to ensure the day ended with the equation ultimately unchanged. Manchester City will still go to Arsenal on Sunday six points behind the reigning champions. They could reduce the gap to three, though the evidence of recent weeks is that it is likelier to stretch to nine. That would surely end City’s title challenge. The theory had been that it would take a potential punishment for their 114 guilty verdicts to do that and, while City are appealing, a sizeable sanction may be still to come. Perhaps that is fitting: the title could be decided on the pitch, rather than in the courts. The temptation is to attribute a slide of three defeats and a draw in four games to off-field matters. Enzo Maresca has denied that is a factor , and whatever his players say in the future, that is overly simplistic. Rather, there are similarities with another side who spiralled from a 100 percent start into a wretched run: Liverpool won their first five matches last season, and then lost four in a row, while City began with seven straight victories a year later. In each case, the initial results came with evidence of flaws which did not halt them: until, suddenly, they did. Neither looked solid defensively or always had the right balance in midfield even when winning . In City’s case, Maresca has lamented a lack of clean sheets, with none in their last nine matches in all competitions, with 26 goals already conceded in the campaign. A new manager does not seem to know his best back four. His habit of making half-time substitutions, with nine in the last nine matches, can show a decisiveness or an inability to find the right formula before then. Some of that is understandable, as Maresca gets used to a squad that was revamped in the summer. The Italian started by impressing with his tactical acumen. Three months into the campaign, however, his team look too susceptible to the counter-attack and offer too little control in midfield. Perhaps it is unfair to criticise Maresca for being too over-reliant on Erling Haaland for goals; it should be a broader concern that, beyond Haaland, Elliot Anderson, Iliman Ndiaye and Rayan Cherki , not too many others are enjoying a fine season personally. Maresca returned to the Etihad Stadium aware of pertinent precedents. He has raised the subject of Manchester United after Sir Alex Ferguson and Arsenal after Arsene Wenger . Neither David Moyes nor Unai Emery mounted a title challenge after replacing a legend. When City touched stratospheric heights under Guardiola, there was always the probability they would decline after him, regardless of the scale of their funding, the legitimacy of those funds or the identity of his successor. top.title: Fred Vasseur furious with latest "unprofessional" Ferrari clash: "It's the same speech as Mexico"
top.description: Motorsport photo Ferrari team boss Fred Vasseur says Charles Leclerc's contact with Lewis Hamilton in the Las Vegas Grand Prix was "unacceptable" and showed "lack of respect for the team", with the Formula 1 team set for fresh crisis talks just three weeks after their spat in Mexico. Vasseur had to hold talks with both Leclerc and Hamilton for their costly Mexico skirmish and will do so again after his two cars tangled on the streets of Las Vegas on lap 38, with Leclerc to blame for leaving his front wing dangling on the inside of Hamilton, sending the Briton into a spin. Leclerc received a 10-second penalty for the collision, while Hamilton dropped to 10th and eventually crossed the line in eighth. Leclerc was classified in 10th place after the penalty had been added to his race time. Coming so soon after Mexico, the thought of his drivers tangling again and the prospect of fresh talks to clear the air had worn thin on Vasseur. "Charles, I want to see you at the end of the race, before anything else," Vasseur said on the team radio during the cooldown lap. When asked what that discussion was like, Vasseur tellingly replied: "It was not a discussion. I spoke. "I think he apologised, he understood, but the result is there. You make a mistake, you say: 'My mistake, I'm sorry'. But you [still] made a mistake." Frederic Vasseur, Ferrari Frederic Vasseur, Ferrari He added: "It's unacceptable. It's a lack of respect for the team, for the sponsors, the same speech as after Mexico. I think we had a clear discussion in Sao Paulo. Today it wasn't professional. I think it's probably the escalation of tension." Following complaints from Hamilton, Ferrari had already been in touch with Leclerc about the aggressive way he was squeezing the Briton. Las Vegas' oval-like slipstreaming race required a degree of trust and teamwork for drivers to move through the pack of cars, as not racing each other was not an option either. The race became a painful reminder that trust between Leclerc and Hamilton is absent. "We passed the message to Charles during the race to think about the team when he was fighting in the right way, but you can't freeze the position on this kind of race, because you are in the slipstream," Vasseur explained. "If you slow down, the guy who is behind you is overtaking you. And all the other teams were able to overtake each other 20 times during the race. You can't imagine the frustration for me, but more important for all the guys at home." top.title: Verstappen wins extraordinary race as Ferraris collide
top.description: The Las Vegas Grand Prix featured 'yo-yo racing' throughout the field with regular overtaking [Reuters] Red Bull's Max Verstappen won an extraordinary Las Vegas Grand Prix that featured 34 lead changes in a non-stop battle at the front. The leading group of 10 cars were tied together for the vast majority of the race as the lead constantly changed hands between Verstappen and the Mercedes drivers George Russell and Kimi Antonelli. But Verstappen was the one constant, always seeming a step ahead of his rivals as he debated electrical energy deployment strategy with his team. And in the final laps Mercedes' challenge unravelled as first Russell made a mistake and crashed trying to pass Antonelli, and the Italian lost out to the two McLarens of Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri going into the final lap. The world champion dropped to fifth going on to the Strip on the last lap but was able to reclaim the place from Alpine's Pierre Gasly at the end of the long straight. And there was more drama at Ferrari as Charles Leclerc earned a 10-second penalty for tipping Lewis Hamilton into a spin. Earlier, Hamilton had been given a 10-second penalty of his own for passing Norris off the track in a fight for position that also involved Leclerc. It was a grand prix more reminiscent of American oval racing than Formula 1, and it depended on unique circumstances revolving around the Las Vegas circuit and energy-starved hybrid engines this year. But there was no questioning the showbiz value in the city that prides itself as the entertainment capital of the world. The key stories of an engrossing race were: Verstappen's remarkable intelligence and control in the lead in the most demanding of circumstances Another dip in a dreadful season for Russell More controversy at Ferrari, as both drivers earned 10-second penalties for driving infringements in battles involving the other Verstappen in control despite lead changes Challengers came and went but Max Verstappen was never without the lead for long in Las Vegas [Getty Images] "How many overtakes did I do?" Verstappen asked his engineer on the slowing down lap, as he reflected on a race the like of which F1 has not seen since the famous Monza slipstreaming battles of the 1960s and early 1970s. "Yeah, and not many of them on the straight," his new engineer Tom Hart said, summing up how Verstappen had secured the win against the Mercedes challenge. Lap after lap after lap, Verstappen, who started from pole, would lose the lead to Russell on the Strip only to reclaim it at the last corner, usually going around the outside. If that did not work, and Russell passed later in the lap, or led across the line, Verstappen developed a trademark move around the outside of Turn Three to get back in front. top.title: First-Class degree not enough to make excellent teacher – TRCN
top.description: The Teachers Registration Council of Nigeria (TRCN) says possessing a first-class degree does not automatically make an individual an excellent teacher. Dr. Ronke Soyombo, Registrar/Chief Executive of TRCN, stated this in an interview with Newsmen on Sunday in Abuja. Soyombo stressed the importance of professional competence adding that effective teaching required more than academic qualifications. The registrar explained that teachers must demonstrate competence in five critical areas assessed through the Council’s professional qualifying examination. She identified the areas as basic mathematics, foundational literacy, digital literacy, pedagogy, and safeguarding and child protection. According to her, teachers must possess a sound understanding of basic mathematical concepts to effectively support children’s learning and development. She described foundational literacy as equally important, noting that strong literacy skills enabled teachers to support learning across other subject areas. The registrar said teachers must also understand today’s children, particularly those belonging to the Alpha Generation, and the technological environment in which they operate. She identified digital literacy as the third major area of assessment, describing it as compulsory for teachers seeking to engage effectively with contemporary learners. To illustrate the challenge, Soyombo recalled visiting an examination centre where she encountered an elderly teacher struggling with a computer mouse. “I remember visiting an examination centre recently and meeting an elderly teacher who held a computer mouse and asked me, ‘Madam, what am I going to do with this?’” she said. She said the encounter highlighted the extent of digital literacy challenges confronting some teachers and raised concerns about their preparedness for modern classrooms. “How can teachers effectively engage children in today’s classrooms if they are not comfortable with basic technology?” she asked. Soyombo, however, acknowledged the challenges and disclosed that several training programmes were being implemented to improve teachers’ digital competence. On pedagogy, she said possessing excellent academic qualifications did not automatically translate into the ability to teach effectively. “Having a first-class degree does not automatically make someone an excellent teacher,” she said. She explained that academic qualifications alone could not guarantee that a teacher understood how to apply appropriate instructional methods to address different learning needs. According to her, classrooms comprise learners with varying abilities, including average pupils, children requiring additional support, and gifted and talented learners. top.title: Zaire Franklin shares unbelievable details of broken leg as Packers await his return
top.description: Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images Green Bay Packers linebacker Zaire Franklin has revealed that he completed two more periods of practice despite suffering a broken leg in what he described as a ‘freak accident’. The defensive captain returned to the field for the first time since fracturing his shin during practice, with his absence leaving a gap in Green Bay’s linebacker unit. Franklin had missed four consecutive games after initially believing the collision was nothing more than a dead leg. However, an X-ray later confirmed the extent of the damage. Zaire Franklin reveals he practised on a broken leg after Green Bay Packers injury Speaking about the incident, Franklin explained how an unusual collision left him with a fracture that he initially struggled to believe. “Somebody just kind of kneed me in a weird way. I’m thinking it’s just dead leg. I actually finished practice. I practiced two more periods on a broken leg,” Franklin said, according to ESPN’s Rob Demovsky. The 30-year-old was stunned when the X-ray revealed the injury, admitting: “And then once I got the X-ray and it was broke, I was looking like, I almost couldn’t believe it. It just looked fake.” Franklin’s injury was particularly frustrating given his previous record of availability. He had missed only one game through injury during his first eight NFL seasons before sitting out four straight contests this season. “The only thing that was going through my mind was, ‘D***, I can’t practice tomorrow?’ It’s been a journey but I’m glad we were able to push through,” he added. “Thank God for keeping my head down and really been leaning on my family. I’m just glad to be back.” Franklin recorded 41 tackles, one forced fumble and one pass defensed in six starts before his injury. He was also named a season-long captain in his first year with Green Bay after holding the same responsibility with the Indianapolis Colts for six consecutive seasons. His return comes at a useful time for the Packers, who have already lost Edgerrin Cooper to a season-ending Achilles injury. Head coach Matt LaFleur expects Franklin to participate on a limited basis, leaving his availability for the Rams clash dependent on how he progresses through the week. top.title: The Daily Hilario: ¡Vamos Republic!
top.description: Nov 21, 2026; Sacramento, CA, USA; Sacramento Republic FC celebrates winning the USL Championship against the Louisville City FC at Sacramento's Heart Health Park. Mandatory Credit: Scott Marshall-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Turned out to be a fun day of sports yesterday … away from the clownshoes of Chelsea that is. The USL Championship game was held yesterday, to determine the winner of America’s second rate soccer league. The league follows the standard US format of a regular season then playoffs, and my local team made it to the final for the second time in their history — a long twelve years after the first time (feels just like yesterday). The fun part about the Championship game is that it’s not at a neutral site, so The Republic got to have home field advantage just like back in 2012. That advantage was sapped a bit by the awkward kick-off time (12pm EST; 9am local) and the freezing temperatures of an early NorCal winter, but an advantage was eventually had. The Republic took the lead and generally dominated the game from start to finish, but the visitors capitalized on a rare error from the captain to equalize and then continued to threaten occasionally on the counter. The only real question was whether they could be broken down. The answer was, no. Thankfully, the penalty shootout swung the home team’s way — Sacramento’s stalvart goalkeeper, Danny Vitiello making two saves and taking Man of the Match honors — and we got to celebrate a second championship for the city. Fireworks and trophy lift in the daytime? Gotta be USL! (Fun fact: the USL have grand plans to establish a new top division to rival MLS, with the added feature of proper promotion/relegation. That’s slated to start in 2028, should it happen. They only have a handful teams committed to it right now, so we’ll see. Sacramento tried to make MLS expansion happen for many years now, but this may be a more feasible route especially with the new soccer-specific stadium being built as we speak .) And the day was still only halfway over! The afternoon brought even more non-Chelsea-sport joy, with the University of Washington taking down the defending national champions, Indiana in a game of collegiate handegg. It’s been a disappointing season for the Huskies overall, with great summer expectations dashed by injuries, questionable coaching decisions, and inconsistent play (including from some of the biggest stars on the team), but this win does put a bit of shine on things as we head into Bowl season. And then, the nightcap was a rather fun F1 race in Las Vegas. With the championship already decided, everybody was out there just having some fun and passing each other left and right. Even Verstappen was enjoying himself. Talk amongst yourselves.

The Mumbaikar is a product of the BCA-Mafatlal bowling scheme under England fast bowling great Frank Tyson in 1990. The one-time player was once again on media duties at St James’ Park on Saturday night for the Newcastle United 2 Arsenal 2 match. Pat Nevin on BBC Radio Five Live, commenting on the first half moment when Bruno Guimaraes almost headed Arsenal into the lead: “That would have broken a few hearts around here, a great run from Bruno Guimaraes. top.title: How every post-Ferguson Man United boss began their reign ahead of Pochettino's debut
top.description: How every post-Ferguson Man United boss began their reign ahead of Pochettino's debut Mauricio Pochettino begins his reign as Manchester United manager at Liverpool this afternoon. Pochettino has become Manchester United's eighth permanent manager since Sir Alex Ferguson's retirement in 2013, and the third in the last three seasons. The Argentine has been tasked with leading the Red Devils out of the Premier League relegation places, but faces a tough first examination at Anfield. Ahead of his debut, here is how each of Manchester United's post-Ferguson managers did on their first game as permanent manager. David Moyes Manchester United 2-0 Wigan Athletic (Community Shield, 2013) David Moyes was dubbed 'The Chosen One' after being handpicked by Ferguson as his replacement. Moyes's impressive work at Everton over more than a decade had earned him the role and he started with trophy success in the Community Shield . Robin van Persie scored both goals as the Red Devils beat surprise FA Cup winners Wigan at Wembley. Moyes was sacked after only 10 months in charge, with the defending Premier League champions seventh in the table with four games to go. Louis van Gaal Manchester United 1-2 Swansea City (Premier League, 2014) Manchester United sought a proven winner to replace Moyes, as Louis van Gaal arrived at Old Trafford. A seven-time title winner across three different leagues, Van Gaal's reign began with defeat. Swansea stunned Manchester United to hand the Red Devils their first home defeat on the opening day of the league season since 1972. It was also the first time that Swansea had won a league game at Old Trafford. Van Gaal spent two seasons with the club and won the FA Cup is second campaign, but was dismissed as United turned to Jose Mourinho . Jose Mourinho Manchester United 2-1 Leicester City (Community Shield, 2016) Jose Mourinho took the reins from Van Gaal and began in trademark Mourinho fashion, with a trophy. Summer signing Zlatan Ibrahimovic scored the winner as Manchester United beat Leicester City to win the Community Shield. United won the League Cup and Europa League during Mourinho's first season, but it proved to be a false dawn in terms of silverware success. Ole Gunnar Solskjaer Manchester United 2-1 Watford (Premier League, 2019) In need of stability after the Mourinho era ended in toxic fashion, former favourite Ole Gunnar Solskjaer took charge on an interim basis. A 5-1 thrashing of Cardiff in his first game started a brilliant spell, which earned Solskjaer the permanent position. The Norwegian's first game as permanent manager was a 2-1 win over Watford, with Marcus Rashford and Anthony Martial on target. Erik ten Hag Manchester United 1-2 Brighton (Premier League, 2022) Erik ten Hag had a debut to forget as Pascal Gross' first-half double saw Brighton beat Manchester United at Old Trafford. top.title: Lewis Hamilton: With No. 1 driver backing, we could have beaten Kimi Antonelli to F1 title
top.description: Motorsport photo Seven-time Formula 1 champion Lewis Hamilton believes he could have beaten Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli in their battle earlier in the season had he been given more support from Ferrari . The Briton was speaking after the Las Vegas Grand Prix, where he had another clash with his team-mate Charles Leclerc , which sent him into a spin. He recovered to finish seventh , while Leclerc was penalised and finished 10th. Asked about 1996 F1 champion Damon Hill's suggestion that Ferrari should make him its number one driver, Hamilton said he had never asked for that status, but felt he had needed it earlier in the year. "I've never asked to be number one. I genuinely haven't ever asked," Hamilton said. He pointed to a stage of the season when he was well clear of Leclerc and the nearest driver to challenge Antonelli for the title. "I was second for a long time in the year, and at that point I needed backing to make sure we beat Kimi. There were a few circumstances in the season where, with the support, we could have beaten Kimi," he said. After the 41-year-old claimed his first grand prix win with Ferrari in Barcelona in June, he was second in the drivers' standings , 41 points behind Antonelli and 40 points ahead of Leclerc. He was also second after Monaco, Belgium and Hungary. Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari, Charles Leclerc, Ferrari Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari, Charles Leclerc, Ferrari Antonelli went on to secure the championship at the Mexican Grand Prix, one week before Mercedes won the constructors' title, and now has 402 points to Hamilton's 267. "I don't know, but it's not something I want to get into," he said when asked where his relationship with his team-mate goes from here. "These are questions that people are asking. At the end of the day, I performed as hard as I could, and I've been giving everything I could to get those points today. "We were just constantly hit with challenges, and I just kept my head down." Earlier in the race, Hamilton had been handed a 10-second penalty for leaving the track and gaining an advantage over McLaren's Lando Norris . "10 seconds was insane and very, very harsh," he continued. "I was avoiding colliding with them, and they could have just told me to give the place back. A 10-second [penalty] is nuts. But I came back and I got back into the fight, and I could see Max up ahead and I was like, we're back in the fight. "I was fighting with McLaren , so I honestly thought that I could maybe fight for a podium, and I'm literally only thinking about fighting McLaren, because that's where we need to be to get the second." nigeria.title: First-Class degree not enough to make excellent teacher – TRCN
nigeria.description: The Teachers Registration Council of Nigeria (TRCN) says possessing a first-class degree does not automatically make an individual an excellent teacher. Dr. Ronke Soyombo, Registrar/Chief Executive of TRCN, stated this in an interview with Newsmen on Sunday in Abuja. Soyombo stressed the importance of professional competence adding that effective teaching required more than academic qualifications. The registrar explained that teachers must demonstrate competence in five critical areas assessed through the Council’s professional qualifying examination. She identified the areas as basic mathematics, foundational literacy, digital literacy, pedagogy, and safeguarding and child protection. According to her, teachers must possess a sound understanding of basic mathematical concepts to effectively support children’s learning and development. She described foundational literacy as equally important, noting that strong literacy skills enabled teachers to support learning across other subject areas. The registrar said teachers must also understand today’s children, particularly those belonging to the Alpha Generation, and the technological environment in which they operate. She identified digital literacy as the third major area of assessment, describing it as compulsory for teachers seeking to engage effectively with contemporary learners. To illustrate the challenge, Soyombo recalled visiting an examination centre where she encountered an elderly teacher struggling with a computer mouse. “I remember visiting an examination centre recently and meeting an elderly teacher who held a computer mouse and asked me, ‘Madam, what am I going to do with this?’” she said. She said the encounter highlighted the extent of digital literacy challenges confronting some teachers and raised concerns about their preparedness for modern classrooms. “How can teachers effectively engage children in today’s classrooms if they are not comfortable with basic technology?” she asked. Soyombo, however, acknowledged the challenges and disclosed that several training programmes were being implemented to improve teachers’ digital competence. On pedagogy, she said possessing excellent academic qualifications did not automatically translate into the ability to teach effectively. “Having a first-class degree does not automatically make someone an excellent teacher,” she said. She explained that academic qualifications alone could not guarantee that a teacher understood how to apply appropriate instructional methods to address different learning needs. According to her, classrooms comprise learners with varying abilities, including average pupils, children requiring additional support, and gifted and talented learners. nigeria.description: The COP31 presidency proposed an eleventh-hour deal Sunday that again fails to mention fossil fuels — an omission that deepened a tense standoff at the UN climate talks. The latest offering by summit co-hosts Turkey and Australia published deep into overtime leaves unresolved tensions over planet-heating fossil fuels but retains a much-sought goal to electrify the global economy. The proposal needs consensus approval from nearly 200 nations at a closing session Sunday but they have struggled to bridge differences during two weeks of grinding negotiations. The European Union and other nations have pushed for strong language on transitioning away from fossil fuels, a call that has faced resistance from oil-rich Saudi Arabia. An EU official told AFP the latest proposal was a “backwards” step, warning there was a “very real possibility” that COP31 ends with no deal. “I am more pessimistic today than I was yesterday,” the official said on condition of anonymity. “The situation is difficult, and the outcome is uncertain. The oil-producing countries are putting up a fierce fight,” a German official said. A Saudi official declined to comment when approached by AFP. Fossil fuels are a flashpoint at the climate talks and the summit comes against a difficult backdrop of soaring energy prices and geopolitical tensions stemming from the war in Iran. A draft deal unveiled earlier this week called for a faster phase out of fossil fuels but a second, pared-down version released Thursday stripped away all mentions of coal, oil and gas. Threats of a walkout prompted Turkey and Australia to convene a hurried meeting between the European Union and Saudi Arabia in a bid to broker a compromise. The latest text introduces a reference to a previous global deal in 2023 to shift the world away from fossil fuels — but stops short of naming them explicitly. And it retains a contentious push to expand carbon capture and storage, a technology championed by the fossil fuel industry but criticised as costly and ineffective in cutting emissions. “We are very disappointed with how the text looks,” the environment minister of Antigua and Barbuda, Michael Joseph, told AFP after leaving the COP31 presidency’s offices. “I can’t honestly say that I’m okay with it passing” in its current state, Joseph said, adding that the draft was “quite silent” on fossil fuels. – Goal to electrify – The draft also calls for global efforts to boost the share of electricity in total final energy consumption to 35 percent by 2035 and the expansion of “clean energy”. The summit had been under pressure to show progress in tackling soaring greenhouse gas emissions in a year of climate-linked disasters from Europe to Nepal and Indonesia. nigeria.title: Messi deserved red card for throwing ball at opponent, says Columbus coach
nigeria.description: Columbus Crew coach Laurent Courtois said Lionel Messi should have been sent off after hurling a throw-in at an opponent as Inter Miami crashed to a 3-0 defeat in the MLS Cup playoffs on Saturday. Messi’s frustration boiled over on the stroke of half-time when he aimed a forceful throw-in into the face of Columbus Crew forward Gonzalo Tapia with 10-man Miami trailing 1-0 at the time. Messi and Tapia both were shown yellow cards for the incident by referee Allen Chapman, but Courtois said afterwards the Argentina superstar should have been given a red card. “Everybody knows that he deserved more than a yellow card,” Courtois said in a post-game press conference when asked about the incident. “It’s just really sad.” Referee Chapman later defended the decision to only show Messi a yellow. “The force used was negligible and the offense did not reach the level of violent conduct,” Chapman told a pool reporter. Inter Miami had already been reduced to 10 men when the incident occurred and were 1-0 down after Chile international Tapia’s early penalty. Reigning MLS champions Miami went on to suffer a 3-0 defeat, with Tapia grabbing a second after a Taha Habroune strike just after half-time at Miami’s Nu Stadium. The result means seventh seeds Columbus, the 2023 champions, can eliminate Messi and Miami from the playoffs with a victory in game two of the best-of-three series in Ohio next Friday. “It was a game where nothing went right for us, and we effectively created their chances for them,” Miami coach Kily Gonzalez said afterwards. “We didn’t produce the great performance we had hoped for. Everything went wrong, but we have to learn from it because next time, if we don’t win, we’re out,” he added. “There’s no better challenge for us as a team than this. It’s a test of character, and I know my team has that character.” In other MLS playoff action on Saturday, Joaquin Valiente scored two goals as host Dallas beat Portland 3-0 in their Western Conference series opener. The 25-year-old Uruguayan midfielder scored in the 53rd and 55th minutes and Samuel Sarver added an insurance goal in the fourth minute of stoppage time for Dallas, who can advance by winning at Portland next Saturday. US teen Peyton Miller scored one goal and set up another in New England’s 2-0 victory over visiting Philadelphia. Miller’s 10th-minute shot deflected in off Philadelphia defender Nathan Harriel to make it 1-0 and the 19-year-old scored in the 73rd minute off a Jack Harrison cross to complete the scoring. New England can advance to the MLS Eastern Conference semi-finals with a road victory next Saturday. It reaffirmed its commitment to sustaining intelligence-driven operations in collaboration with other security agencies to eliminate threats to lives and property. entertainment.title: Asali Africa: Serves Up ‘There’s Rice at Home’ A New Cooking Series Hosted by Chef Soliat Bada
entertainment.description: Chef Soliat Bada Anyone who grew up in a Nigerian home knows the line. You suggest buying food outside, and before you finish the sentence, someone reminds you that there’s rice at home. It is usually the end of the conversation. In Asali Africa’s new series, it is where the conversation starts. There’s Rice at Home is a cooking and conversation show from Asali Africa, the Lagos-based creative development agency, hosted by Chef Soliat Bada . In each episode, Soliat cooks one rice dish with a guest, and while the pot does its work, the two get into the kind of talk that usually happens around food: family, money and what success really looks like. Rice is the most ordinary thing in a Nigerian kitchen, and the show makes a good case that it doesn’t have to taste ordinary. Over five episodes, released every two weeks, the menu travels from Jamaica to Saudi Arabia, back home to Nigeria and on to Louisiana. You don’t just watch the food get made, either. The recipes are written up in full on Asali Africa’s website, with the ingredients and method laid out step by step, so you can watch Soliat cook a dish and then make it in your own kitchen. The season opens with Rice and Peas with Oxtail, the Jamaican Sunday staple of rice cooked in coconut milk with red kidney beans (the “peas”), served beside rich, slow-cooked oxtail. Soliat’s guest is Michael Famoroti , co-founder of Stears, and their conversation turns to family and black tax: the expectation that once you start earning, you start supporting the people who raised you. entertainment.description: The presence of Mini LED tells a shopper something important about the light source behind an LCD panel. It does not, by itself, explain how that light is arranged, divided or controlled. Those implementation choices can have a major influence on contrast, black level performance, highlight control and the visibility of blooming in difficult scenes. From Presence To Performance That distinction matters because a category becomes more useful to consumers when it can be evaluated through clear performance principles rather than through a technology name alone. For Mini LED, three factors provide a practical starting point. The first is hardware local dimming. In a hardware based system, physical groups of LEDs can be brightened, dimmed or switched off independently across different areas of the screen. This gives the television more direct control over how light is distributed within a single image. The second is local dimming zone count and precision. A higher number of independently controlled zones can allow the backlight to respond in smaller areas, which can improve separation between bright highlights and surrounding dark regions when other major conditions are comparable. The number itself is not the whole story, but it is a useful indicator of how granular the backlight system can be. The third is backlight architecture. Full Array Local Dimming places controllable zones across the area behind the panel, providing the physical foundation for more localized light management than designs that illuminate the panel from the edges or operate the backlight more uniformly. Together, these three elements move the Mini LED conversation from a simple question of whether the technology is present to a more useful question: how effectively is the light being controlled? Where TCL Enters The Category Conversation TCL is relevant to that discussion because Mini LED has become a significant part of its global television business. According to Omdia data cited in TCL Electronics interim results, TCL ranked No. 1 globally by Mini LED TV shipment volume in the first half of 2026. TCL reported 2.43 million Mini LED TV shipments during the period, representing 77.1% year on year growth. That position follows a strong 2025, when TCL reported, based on Omdia data, a 31.1% share of global Mini LED TV shipments and 118.0% year on year shipment growth. entertainment.title: A Safari, a Beach & Easy Entry? 5 African Spots for Your Christmas Holiday
entertainment.description: Five African destinations Nigerian passport holders can visit visa-free or with visa on arrival this Christmas holiday. Image: AI-generated. The group chat has the concerts, the dinners and the Detty December link-ups covered. But has anyone planned the getaway? Beyond the usual Lagos parties and end-of-year outings, there is a whole continent waiting to be explored, with sun-soaked beaches, wildlife safaris, exciting food scenes and cities with plenty of stories to tell. You do not have to spend weeks navigating embassy appointments and visa applications to make it happen, either. Several African countries offer Nigerian passport holders visa-free entry or visas on arrival, making a festive-season escape much easier to plan. Whether you are travelling solo, gathering your friends, taking the family along or joining a curated travel group, here are five destinations worth considering for your Christmas holiday. Kenya Imagine spotting lions and giraffes against a city skyline before breakfast, then catching an evening flight or train straight to the coast for fresh seafood by the Indian Ocean. That contrast is what makes Kenya such a rewarding December escape. Nairobi gives you immediate access to wildlife at Nairobi National Park and the Giraffe Centre alongside lively restaurants and art spaces in Westlands and Karen, while longer itineraries open up classic game drives in the Maasai Mara, views of Mount Kilimanjaro in Amboseli, and warm beach days in Diani or Watamu. He was so convinced that I wondered whether a manual somewhere explained how men were manufactured. According to him, men were created to be strong, endure pain and keep their emotions to themselves. That was simply how they were made. “So, because you’re a man, you’re not supposed to feel hurt, fear or disappointment?” I disagreed. He insisted that showing emotions was not in a man’s nature. Who made that rule? Who decided that men could experience pain but must never be seen expressing it? At what point did being a man become synonymous with pretending that everything was fine? The conversation wilted, but it has stayed with me, perhaps because my friend wasn’t expressing an unusual opinion. He was repeating a stereotype many of us have heard all our lives: “Boys don’t cry.” “Be a man.” “Man up.” Three little expressions, and somewhere between being told to be strong and learning to say “I’m fine,” I wonder how many men have forgotten what it feels like to be heard. Work nko?” “When are you getting married?” “Have you bought land?” “How is the family?” And the famous Nigerian question that can make an unemployed graduate dread family gatherings: “So, what are you doing now?” We often inquire about their achievements, responsibilities, and plans. These aspects are important, but how often do we ask about their fears? A father who leaves home before sunrise and returns exhausted, burdened by the weight of school fees, rent, and family expectations. A young graduate who has submitted countless job applications, yet still smiles politely when another relative inquires why he hasn’t found a job. A successful professional whose LinkedIn profile showcases numerous achievements, while his personal life tells a story that no one has thought to ask about. We admire their strength, we applaud their sacrifices, and we celebrate their accomplishments. But what about what they are going through? The person everyone leans on also needs somewhere to lean. Whenever I went to work, he would come to pick me up from the office, and we would go home together. In many ways, he looked out for me and made sure I got home safely. We started talking more. But then would I have done that out of genuine affection or simply out of pity? And would that have been fair to either of us? My understanding is that not returning someone’s romantic feelings does not mean we cannot offer them genuine friendship, kindness and compassion. entertainment.title: Visa Report Identifies Opportunity to Integrate Digital Payments with SMEs Business Operations in Nigeria
entertainment.description: Report identifies next SME digitization opportunity: connecting payments with day-to-day business management. 94% of SMEs surveyed find an all-in-one payment and business solution appealing, yet only 29% currently use one, pointing to untapped demand for tools that connect payments with business management. Integrated payment and business solutions can give financial institutions a more holistic view of SME cash flow and support more tailored financing solutions over time. Small- and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in Nigeria have largely moved beyond the first stage of digital payment adoption, but a productivity gap remains. According to Visa’s new survey for its Pay and Get Paid 2026 report, most of the SMEs surveyed in Nigeria use digital payments, showing how firmly digital commerce has taken root in the country’s small business economy. However, many SMEs still manage the related financial and operational tasks separately, with only 29% currently using an integrated solution that connects payments with broader business management. The report shows that financial admin and disconnected tools create friction for SMEs, with surveyed businesses citing challenges in tracking outstanding invoices (14%), keeping payroll records organized (19%), and preparing financial reports (16%). These pain points reflect a disconnect between payments and the operational tasks that follow, with some businesses juggling multiple systems to keep their business running. The appetite for a more connected approach is clear. According to the report, 94% of SMEs find an all-in-one payment and business solution appealing, reflecting strong interest in tools that can bring payments and key business operations into one experience. However, adoption has yet to catch up: only 29% of SMEs currently use an integrated payment and business platform. The report points to several perception barriers that may be slowing adoption. Businesses cited that they already have manual processes that work (8%), that an integrated platform may disrupt their current way of working (8%), or that they do not trust relying on a single provider (7%). These findings suggest that broader adoption will depend on helping SMEs better understand how integrated tools can be relevant, accessible, and scalable for businesses at different stages of growth. At the same time, the experience of SMEs already using integrated solutions suggests a strong value case. The report found that Nigerian businesses using an integrated tool or platform report 93% satisfaction, with 88% reporting efficiency gains, including reductions in the time and effort required to manage their business. Beyond efficiency, integrated platforms may also create new opportunities for financial institutions to deepen SME relationships by using richer payments and business-management data to better understand cash flow patterns, support risk assessment, and potentially enable more relevant lending solutions over time. In June 2023, ahead of the 66th Grammy Awards, the Recording Academy announced the creation of the Best African Music Performance category. Its creation was a recognition of how far African music had travelled globally, and Nigerian artists were at the centre of that movement. From Burna Boy ‘s Ye , CKay ‘s Love Nwantiti , Wizkid ‘s explosive Essence , to Rema ‘s globally successful Calm Down and others, Nigerian artists became drivers of African music’s global expansion. Afrobeats – the umbrella term often used internationally to describe much of contemporary African popular music, although many Nigerian artists have rejected it for its tendency to limit the range of music coming out of the country – became an established genre globally. While Nigerian and African music have always travelled beyond their respective countries, the era of streaming and digital platforms has accelerated how quickly global audiences discover and engage with the music. African music became increasingly established in the West and other parts of the world, creating greater recognition for its artists and sounds. The Grammys’ decision to introduce a category specifically recognising African music performances was an important step in that direction, beyond the recognition African artists had previously received in categories such as Best Global Music Album. Although the creation of the Best African Music Performance category was celebrated throughout the continent, there seems to be a monopoly, or something close to it, of Nigerian music in the category. Indeed, Nigerian artists are considerably more recognised globally, particularly in the West. sports.description: Leeds United head-wrecking crew stay the right side of crazy at Chelsea - Graham Smyth's Verdict It's good to be just the right side of crazy. More often than not Leeds United Football Club finds itself involved in mayhem. That is an apt word for so much of all that has happened to and around this club since its very inception in 1919. There's been good crazy and bad crazy, everything from the daft to the scarcely believable. Leeds United is a club that rarely needs a second invitation to lose the run of itself. Even under the calm managerial control of Daniel Farke and the sober ownership of 49ers Enterprises, minds have melted and chaos has briefly reigned at times. Take, for example, the last trip to Stamford Bridge, when Leeds lost 6-3. Scorelines like that rarely make sense. That was, in the words of Jayden Bogle, a 'crazy game' and something that he wanted to put right. And what better way to do that than a good old-fashioned historical head-wrecking. It all started with a bit of cat and mouse. Leeds almost played rope-a-dope in the opening stages, seeing relatively little of the football and absorbing pressure. Chelsea saw precious little of James Trafford's goal, because Leeds stayed so compact and patient, looking for opportunities to nip in. Farke's three centre-backs all chipped in with important interventions but almost all of the defending was kept to the edge of the area and further out. It wasn't until the 14th minute that the hosts mustered a shot, Morgan Rogers pulling the trigger from distance and missing the target. Chances to break out were few and far between, but when Leeds did get hold of the ball they moved it well. So well in fact that they created two good opportunities to open the scoring. sports.description: Motorsport photo Kean Nakamura-Berta claimed a comfortable Macau Grand Prix victory after forcing early leader Enzo Deligny into a mistake at Lisboa. It was a tricky first few corners for the drivers starting on the front row as second-placed Mattia Colnaghi struggled to get away, while polesitter Rashid Al Dhaheri was immediately under attack. Deligny braved it around the outside of the Mercedes junior at Mandarin to grab the lead, before Al Dhaheri then lost out to both Nakamura-Berta and Yuki Sano on the run to Lisboa. Williams junior Nakamura-Berta spent the next couple of laps putting Deligny under pressure before a brief safety car period was triggered when ninth-placed Reza Seewooruthun was tapped into the barriers out of Mandarin by last year's F4 World Cup winner Jules Roussel. Nakamura-Berta continued to remain about half a second behind Deligny upon the restart until he suddenly closed on lap 10 of 16. The SJM Theodore Racing driver was right on the tail of Deligny on the run to Lisboa and the leader left his braking as late as he dared but it was too late and he ploughed into the barriers. This gifted Nakamura-Berta a huge 3.5s lead, which enabled him to stroke it home to the flag to take the victory. The British-born Japanese, Slovak driver, who was third in this year's Formula Regional European Championship standings, made up for the disappointment of crashing out of the F4 World Cup last year. His large margin was aided by R-ace GP driver Al Dhaheri spending several laps bottled up behind Sano's TOM'S Formula Regional machine. The qualification race winner eventually found a way through around the outside of Mandarin on lap 12 but there was too much for him to do to close on Nakamura-Berta in the remaining three tours. Alex Ninovic Alex Ninovic Alex Ninovic made a similar move on Sano at Mandarin on the following lap to return to his starting spot of third on the grid. The 2025 GB3 champion then set about battling Al Dhaheri, blasting ahead on the run to Mandarin on the final lap to finish second, 2.456s behind the winner. Nakamura-Berta's team-mate James Egozi also passed Sano in the closing stages to seal fourth. sports.description: The best part of five hours after the final whistle blew at the Etihad Stadium and about 150 miles north east, Noni Madueke scored an equaliser to ensure the day ended with the equation ultimately unchanged. Manchester City will still go to Arsenal on Sunday six points behind the reigning champions. They could reduce the gap to three, though the evidence of recent weeks is that it is likelier to stretch to nine. That would surely end City’s title challenge. The theory had been that it would take a potential punishment for their 114 guilty verdicts to do that and, while City are appealing, a sizeable sanction may be still to come. Perhaps that is fitting: the title could be decided on the pitch, rather than in the courts. The temptation is to attribute a slide of three defeats and a draw in four games to off-field matters. Enzo Maresca has denied that is a factor , and whatever his players say in the future, that is overly simplistic. Rather, there are similarities with another side who spiralled from a 100 percent start into a wretched run: Liverpool won their first five matches last season, and then lost four in a row, while City began with seven straight victories a year later. In each case, the initial results came with evidence of flaws which did not halt them: until, suddenly, they did. Neither looked solid defensively or always had the right balance in midfield even when winning . In City’s case, Maresca has lamented a lack of clean sheets, with none in their last nine matches in all competitions, with 26 goals already conceded in the campaign. A new manager does not seem to know his best back four. His habit of making half-time substitutions, with nine in the last nine matches, can show a decisiveness or an inability to find the right formula before then. Some of that is understandable, as Maresca gets used to a squad that was revamped in the summer. The Italian started by impressing with his tactical acumen. sports.title: Verstappen wins extraordinary race as Ferraris collide
sports.description: The Las Vegas Grand Prix featured 'yo-yo racing' throughout the field with regular overtaking [Reuters] Red Bull's Max Verstappen won an extraordinary Las Vegas Grand Prix that featured 34 lead changes in a non-stop battle at the front. The leading group of 10 cars were tied together for the vast majority of the race as the lead constantly changed hands between Verstappen and the Mercedes drivers George Russell and Kimi Antonelli. But Verstappen was the one constant, always seeming a step ahead of his rivals as he debated electrical energy deployment strategy with his team. And in the final laps Mercedes' challenge unravelled as first Russell made a mistake and crashed trying to pass Antonelli, and the Italian lost out to the two McLarens of Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri going into the final lap. The world champion dropped to fifth going on to the Strip on the last lap but was able to reclaim the place from Alpine's Pierre Gasly at the end of the long straight. And there was more drama at Ferrari as Charles Leclerc earned a 10-second penalty for tipping Lewis Hamilton into a spin. Earlier, Hamilton had been given a 10-second penalty of his own for passing Norris off the track in a fight for position that also involved Leclerc. It was a grand prix more reminiscent of American oval racing than Formula 1, and it depended on unique circumstances revolving around the Las Vegas circuit and energy-starved hybrid engines this year. But there was no questioning the showbiz value in the city that prides itself as the entertainment capital of the world. The key stories of an engrossing race were: Verstappen's remarkable intelligence and control in the lead in the most demanding of circumstances Another dip in a dreadful season for Russell More controversy at Ferrari, as both drivers earned 10-second penalties for driving infringements in battles involving the other Verstappen in control despite lead changes Challengers came and went but Max Verstappen was never without the lead for long in Las Vegas [Getty Images] "How many overtakes did I do?" Verstappen asked his engineer on the slowing down lap, as he reflected on a race the like of which F1 has not seen since the famous Monza slipstreaming battles of the 1960s and early 1970s. "Yeah, and not many of them on the straight," his new engineer Tom Hart said, summing up how Verstappen had secured the win against the Mercedes challenge. sports.title: Zaire Franklin shares unbelievable details of broken leg as Packers await his return
sports.description: Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images Green Bay Packers linebacker Zaire Franklin has revealed that he completed two more periods of practice despite suffering a broken leg in what he described as a ‘freak accident’. The defensive captain returned to the field for the first time since fracturing his shin during practice, with his absence leaving a gap in Green Bay’s linebacker unit. Franklin had missed four consecutive games after initially believing the collision was nothing more than a dead leg. However, an X-ray later confirmed the extent of the damage. Zaire Franklin reveals he practised on a broken leg after Green Bay Packers injury Speaking about the incident, Franklin explained how an unusual collision left him with a fracture that he initially struggled to believe. “Somebody just kind of kneed me in a weird way. I’m thinking it’s just dead leg. I actually finished practice. I practiced two more periods on a broken leg,” Franklin said, according to ESPN’s Rob Demovsky. The 30-year-old was stunned when the X-ray revealed the injury, admitting: “And then once I got the X-ray and it was broke, I was looking like, I almost couldn’t believe it. It just looked fake.” Franklin’s injury was particularly frustrating given his previous record of availability. He had missed only one game through injury during his first eight NFL seasons before sitting out four straight contests this season. “The only thing that was going through my mind was, ‘D***, I can’t practice tomorrow?’ It’s been a journey but I’m glad we were able to push through,” he added. “Thank God for keeping my head down and really been leaning on my family. sports.title: The Daily Hilario: ¡Vamos Republic!
sports.description: Nov 21, 2026; Sacramento, CA, USA; Sacramento Republic FC celebrates winning the USL Championship against the Louisville City FC at Sacramento's Heart Health Park. Mandatory Credit: Scott Marshall-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Turned out to be a fun day of sports yesterday … away from the clownshoes of Chelsea that is. The USL Championship game was held yesterday, to determine the winner of America’s second rate soccer league. The league follows the standard US format of a regular season then playoffs, and my local team made it to the final for the second time in their history — a long twelve years after the first time (feels just like yesterday). The fun part about the Championship game is that it’s not at a neutral site, so The Republic got to have home field advantage just like back in 2012. That advantage was sapped a bit by the awkward kick-off time (12pm EST; 9am local) and the freezing temperatures of an early NorCal winter, but an advantage was eventually had. The Republic took the lead and generally dominated the game from start to finish, but the visitors capitalized on a rare error from the captain to equalize and then continued to threaten occasionally on the counter. The only real question was whether they could be broken down. The answer was, no. Thankfully, the penalty shootout swung the home team’s way — Sacramento’s stalvart goalkeeper, Danny Vitiello making two saves and taking Man of the Match honors — and we got to celebrate a second championship for the city. Fireworks and trophy lift in the daytime? Gotta be USL! (Fun fact: the USL have grand plans to establish a new top division to rival MLS, with the added feature of proper promotion/relegation. That’s slated to start in 2028, should it happen. They only have a handful teams committed to it right now, so we’ll see. Sacramento tried to make MLS expansion happen for many years now, but this may be a more feasible route especially with the new soccer-specific stadium being built as we speak .) And the day was still only halfway over! The afternoon brought even more non-Chelsea-sport joy, with the University of Washington taking down the defending national champions, Indiana in a game of collegiate handegg. It’s been a disappointing season for the Huskies overall, with great summer expectations dashed by injuries, questionable coaching decisions, and inconsistent play (including from some of the biggest stars on the team), but this win does put a bit of shine on things as we head into Bowl season. And then, the nightcap was a rather fun F1 race in Las Vegas. With the championship already decided, everybody was out there just having some fun and passing each other left and right. Even Verstappen was enjoying himself. Talk amongst yourselves.

sports.title: Paras Mhambrey set to join Punjab Kings as bowling coach
sports.description: MUMBAI: Former India and Mumbai Indians bowling coach Paras Mhambrey is set to join Punjab Kings as their new bowling coach for IPL-2027, TOI has learnt. Punjab Kings had parted ways with their bowling coach James Hopes recently. Mhambrey will thus chalk out bowling strategies with PBKS head coach Ricky Ponting and skipper Shreyas Iyer. He was initially with MI since the IPL’s inception in 2008, and then rejoined MI after completing his tenure with the Indian team following the 2024 T20 World Cup triumph. Mhambrey is currently in Dubai as bowling coach of MI Emirates in the ILT20. He had also coached the India Under-19 team in the 2020 U-19 World Cup in South Africa. During his nearly three-year stint with Team India, the 54-year-old ex-India pacer-turned coach was credited by many, especially ace pacer Mohammed Shami, who kept gesturing towards him from the field during matches, for the Indian bowlers’ brilliant show in the 2023 ODI World Cup in India, and the T20 World Cup in West Indies in June this year. The Mumbaikar is a product of the BCA-Mafatlal bowling scheme under England fast bowling great Frank Tyson in 1990. He then went on to possess a rich 21-year coaching experience in his CV, a period in which he coached multiple domestic teams, including Bengal, Baroda, Maharashtra and Vidarbha.

sports.title: How every post-Ferguson Man United boss began their reign ahead of Pochettino's debut

Pochettino has become Manchester United's eighth permanent manager since Sir Alex Ferguson's retirement in 2013, and the third in the last three seasons. The Argentine has been tasked with leading the Red Devils out of the Premier League relegation places, but faces a tough first examination at Anfield. Ahead of his debut, here is how each of Manchester United's post-Ferguson managers did on their first game as permanent manager. David Moyes Manchester United 2-0 Wigan Athletic (Community Shield, 2013) David Moyes was dubbed 'The Chosen One' after being handpicked by Ferguson as his replacement. Moyes's impressive work at Everton over more than a decade had earned him the role and he started with trophy success in the Community Shield . Robin van Persie scored both goals as the Red Devils beat surprise FA Cup winners Wigan at Wembley. Moyes was sacked after only 10 months in charge, with the defending Premier League champions seventh in the table with four games to go. Louis van Gaal Manchester United 1-2 Swansea City (Premier League, 2014) Manchester United sought a proven winner to replace Moyes, as Louis van Gaal arrived at Old Trafford. A seven-time title winner across three different leagues, Van Gaal's reign began with defeat. Swansea stunned Manchester United to hand the Red Devils their first home defeat on the opening day of the league season since 1972. It was also the first time that Swansea had won a league game at Old Trafford. Van Gaal spent two seasons with the club and won the FA Cup is second campaign, but was dismissed as United turned to Jose Mourinho . sports.title: Lewis Hamilton: With No. 1 driver backing, we could have beaten Kimi Antonelli to F1 title
sports.description: Motorsport photo Seven-time Formula 1 champion Lewis Hamilton believes he could have beaten Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli in their battle earlier in the season had he been given more support from Ferrari . The Briton was speaking after the Las Vegas Grand Prix, where he had another clash with his team-mate Charles Leclerc , which sent him into a spin. He recovered to finish seventh , while Leclerc was penalised and finished 10th. Asked about 1996 F1 champion Damon Hill's suggestion that Ferrari should make him its number one driver, Hamilton said he had never asked for that status, but felt he had needed it earlier in the year. "I've never asked to be number one. I genuinely haven't ever asked," Hamilton said. He pointed to a stage of the season when he was well clear of Leclerc and the nearest driver to challenge Antonelli for the title. "I was second for a long time in the year, and at that point I needed backing to make sure we beat Kimi. There were a few circumstances in the season where, with the support, we could have beaten Kimi," he said. After the 41-year-old claimed his first grand prix win with Ferrari in Barcelona in June, he was second in the drivers' standings , 41 points behind Antonelli and 40 points ahead of Leclerc. He was also second after Monaco, Belgium and Hungary. Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari, Charles Leclerc, Ferrari Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari, Charles Leclerc, Ferrari Antonelli went on to secure the championship at the Mexican Grand Prix, one week before Mercedes won the constructors' title, and now has 402 points to Hamilton's 267. "I don't know, but it's not something I want to get into," he said when asked where his relationship with his team-mate goes from here. "These are questions that people are asking. At the end of the day, I performed as hard as I could, and I've been giving everything I could to get those points today. "We were just constantly hit with challenges, and I just kept my head down." Earlier in the race, Hamilton had been handed a 10-second penalty for leaving the track and gaining an advantage over McLaren's Lando Norris . "10 seconds was insane and very, very harsh," he continued. "I was avoiding colliding with them, and they could have just told me to give the place back. A 10-second [penalty] is nuts. But I came back and I got back into the fight, and I could see Max up ahead and I was like, we're back in the fight. "I was fighting with McLaren , so I honestly thought that I could maybe fight for a podium, and I'm literally only thinking about fighting McLaren, because that's where we need to be to get the second." technology.title: Come for the science, stay for the big iron: Supercomputer admin on why he loves the job
technology.description: Web hosting might seem like an unlikely on-ramp to supercomputer administration, but it set Mark O'Shea on his way to running some of Australia's most powerful machines. O'Shea is team leader for supercomputing operations and senior supercomputing systems administrator at Australia's Pawsey Supercomputing Research Centre . Pawsey is home to Setonix, an HPE Cray EX supercomputer with more than 200,000 AMD EPYC CPU cores and hundreds of AMD Instinct MI250X accelerators. Its GPU partition ranks 87th in the November TOP500 and 37th in the Green500 , which measures computational performance per watt. "Working in web hosting wasn't much different to what I was doing a few years later with supercomputers," O'Shea tells The Register . "Datacenters are essentially several thousand computers, as are supercomputers. "So, we essentially had the same problems," he says, especially as regards cooling and power management. There's no single formal route into supercomputer administration in Australia, O'Shea says. He picked up the necessary skills over time. Andrew Underwood, Dell's chief technology officer for high-performance computing and artificial intelligence across the Asia-Pacific, Japan, and China, says that lack of formal training means some supercomputer admins start in academia. He's observed that many HPC admins emerge from the sciences, catching the computing bug during their studies. A biologist working with a massive genomics database, for example, might discover a taste for running the systems behind it. "The biologist might decide they want to be someone working in IT helping other biologists transform their industry," Underwood says . "One of the things I really admire about people who work in the supercomputing field is they take it so seriously," Underwood adds. "It's almost a passion, a hobby, more so than it is a job." "They want to play that real supporting and foundational role of assisting and engaging with scientists to help them use the technology to solve the problems the world faces." O'Shea agrees, noting that many people who get into supercomputer admin are PhD graduates who stick around their universities after they graduate. Some of them gravitate toward running the departmental computers and then wind up in supercomputing. "There are many roles around universities allowing people to be introduced to [supercomputer administration] while still doing enterprise-style or more departmental admin for researchers and system administration," O'Shea says. Regardless of how a supercomputer admin gets their gig, both O'Shea and Underwood say the supersysadmin community is tight knit – which may not always be a good thing. "As an industry in supercomputing, we need to be open to people from diverse backgrounds," Underwood says, "and we need to build these frameworks like the Student Cluster Competition, conferences like eResearch and the SC Conference, where students can get educated and systems admins get exposed to continual training." Swirls and Colors on Jupiter from Juno Explanation: What creates the colors in Jupiter’s clouds? No one is sure. The thick atmosphere of Jupiter is mostly hydrogen and helium , elements which are colorless at the low temperatures of the Jovian cloud tops . Which trace molecules provide the colors remains a topic of research , although small amounts of ammonium hydrosulfide are one leading candidate . What is clear from the featured color-enhanced image — and many similar images — is that lighter clouds are typically higher up than darker ones. Pictured, light clouds swirl around reddish regions toward the lower right, while they appear to cover over some darker domains on the upper right. The featured image was taken by the robotic Juno spacecraft in 2018 during its 14th low pass over Jupiter . Before Rømer figured it out, scientists thought that light travels instantaneously, or infinitely fast. Rømer disproved this almost by accident when he was studying Jupiter's moon Io . He was trying to figure out how long it takes Io to orbit Jupiter in hopes of using it as a cosmic clock. He watched Io disappear behind Jupiter and reappear on the other side. He did this over and over every 42 hours for years. To his surprise, the timing of the eclipses was not consistent. When Earth was closest to Jupiter, the eclipses happened 11 minutes early. Likewise, when the two planets were farthest away, the eclipses were 11 minutes behind schedule. Rømer figured out the pattern and made an accurate prediction for Io's eclipse on Nov. 9, 1676. Then on Nov. 21, he took his findings to the Royal Academy of Sciences and explained that a finite speed of light must be responsible. Danish astronomer Ole Rømer (Image credit: Wikimedia Commons) Why it mattered Understanding that the speed of light is a constant is the key that opened our ability to gauge the scale of the universe, as well as was central to developing modern physics. "The speed of light becomes a sort of ultimate speed limit," Live Science explained in an article about why the speed of light matters. "In fact, objects with mass, be they cars or neutrinos, can't reach the speed of light because they would need infinite energy to do so."
